gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the parking-mode hardwire kit costs or the battery voltage at which it cuts the camera off, so none shows that the A810 kit ChatGPT calls best lands at $137.97 with 70mai's rear camera and kit while carrying a lithium battery, not the supercapacitor its own answer asks for.
standout_why: Compared against dashpicked.com, dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams, knowledgelib.io and carcody.com (the cited pages I could open) plus productbible.com. All five say parking mode needs a hardwire kit; dashpicked even names 70mai's UP03/UP05/UP06. None gives a kit price or a cutoff voltage, and none adds the kit to the camera price against $150. carcody gets closest ('an always-on fuse connection and a hardwire kit with low-voltage protection') but with no figures. dashcamtalk and knowledgelib already carry the A810 Lite's drop to 24/25 fps with the rear camera, so that part is not new. caranddriver.com (cited) and thecargearguide.com could not be opened, so they are not compared.
decides: It changes the pick only for a shopper who wants parking recording inside the $150. Camera, rear camera and kit together: the Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH comes to $160.98 with its cheapest kit, which is over. The 70mai A810 comes to $137.97 from the three base prices read, but DashCamTalk says it has a 500 mAh lithium battery and drops to 25 fps once the rear camera is attached. The DDPAI Z50 Pro Dual GPS + Hardwire Kit is $159.00 on the store before code SAVEBIGBF; the brief's 12% would make it $139.92 by my arithmetic, which is not cart-tested on this variant. The DDPAI N3 Pro Dual GPS + Hardwire Kit is $109.00 before the code. For a shopper who only records while driving, this finding leaves the pick unchanged.
